svg.title: Kitchen lighting: 12 V RGB minimum breadboard layout
svg.desc: Minimum short-strip experiment using an Arduino Nano 33 IoT, three TN0702N3-G logic-level N-channel MOSFETs, barrel jack J0, and two Würth 615004144121 female RJ11 output jacks J1/J2. RJ11 mounting and pin fan-outs are conceptual, not a physical breadboard footprint. Both jacks connect in parallel: pin 2 positive, pin 3 red, pin 4 green, pin 5 blue. Nano D3, D5 and D6 directly control the red, green and blue MOSFET gates. No gate drivers, resistors or capacitors are installed. Output positive connects to J0 pin 1 by soldered pigtails, bypassing breadboard contacts; row 40 is unused. Both +12 V rails and both ground rails are linked at the top, with bridges across all four midpoint breaks. Nano VIN connects to the left + rail at row 15; Nano GND connects to the right - rail at row 12. Strip returns still pass through breadboard contacts and MOSFETs, never through Nano GPIO. The two ports share a combined 25 cm / 0.30 A LED load limit. All wires are drawn.
svg.text: RGB outputs · ≤25 cm combined · ≤0.30 A total
